Hadar (king of Edom)
HAY-dar
proper noun
Hebrew hadar, “honour” or “ornament” (written Hadad in 1Chr 1:50), the name of the last named king of Edom, of the city Pau.

📖 Biblical Definition

Hadar reigned in Edom after the death of Baal-hanan the son of Achbor, and he is the last named of the kings of Edom in the generations of Esau (Gen 36:39). The name of his city was Pau; and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. He is the only one of these kings whose death is not recorded in the chronicle, and the only one whose wife and her lineage are set down, as though the register pauses at the last to mark the end of the line. In the parallel place he is called Hadad (1Chr 1:50), a small variance of the letters that the diligent reader will not stumble at. His name signifies honour or ornament; yet the honour of Edom was a fading flower, for after these kings the rule passed to the dukes, and at the last to the desolation pronounced by the prophets. As for Edom, I will lay it desolate (Eze 35:15); and, They shall call it, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever (Mal 1:4). Hadar’s honour was but for a season. The Holy Ghost closes the catalogue of Edom’s kings with a marriage and a city, then turns the page to the dukes and to the doom; but Israel’s King is crowned with honour that fadeth not, and His name endureth for ever.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Hadar (called Hadad in 1Chr 1:50) of Pau, the last named king of Edom, after Baal-hanan (Gen 36:39).

expand to see more

HADAR, of the city Pau, the last named king who reigned in the land of Edom.

He reigned after the death of Baal-hanan the son of Achbor (Gen 36:39).

His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

He is called Hadad in the parallel chronicle of the kings (1Chr 1:50).

He closes the line of Edom’s kings, after whom the rule passed to the dukes.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 36:39 — "And Baalhanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pau; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab."

Mal 1:3 — "And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness."

Gen 36:31 — "And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel."

Heb 12:16 — "Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A king of the genealogical record, not a contested doctrine; Hadar, last of Edom’s kings, witnesses to the fading honour of Esau’s house, soon laid waste by the LORD.

expand to see more

Hadar of Pau is a figure of the sacred register, the last named king of Edom, whose wife and her lineage alone are recorded among these kings. No movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him; the dictionary records him that the reader may know him for a real king who closes the line, and that Hadar and Hadad are one name in the two registers.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the brevity of all worldly honour against the everlasting honour of God’s King. Hadar’s name means honour, yet Edom’s honour faded, and the LORD laid Esau’s heritage waste (Mal 1:3). Esau was profane (Heb 12:16). The catalogue of Edom’s kings ends with a marriage and a desolation; but Israel’s King is crowned with honour that fadeth not.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “honour” or “ornament,” Hadar names the last king of Edom, of Pau, called Hadad in Chronicles.

expand to see more

Hadar — Hebrew hadar, “honour” or “ornament.”

He came of the city Pau, the last named king of Edom (Gen 36:39).

His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

He is called Hadad in the parallel record (1Chr 1:50).

After him the rule of Edom passed from kings to dukes.

Usage

"Hadar’s name means honour, yet the honour of Edom was a fading flower."

"His is the last crown in Edom’s line, soon followed by the prophets’ doom."

"Israel’s King is crowned with honour that fadeth not, and His name endureth for ever."
